1.titulo: Note with bibliographic references on African topics.
1.descricao: Notes written by Jaime Batalha Reis, Portuguese economist and literary critic, containing bibliographic sources on the history of Africa.

2.descricao: Notes written by Jaime Batalha Reis, Portuguese economist and literary critic, with brief descriptions of the Bantu peoples.
2.area: History of Africa, Bantu People, Central Africa

3.titulo: Newspaper clipping from “Comércio Português” entitled “England’s civilizing processes”.
3.descricao: The report denounces instruments of torture used by the African Lakes Company mission. The denunciation was made by the explorers Capello and Ivens when they returned to Lisbon after crossing from Angola to the opposite coast.
3.area: Slavery, Torture, Colonization, Angola, Central Africa

4.titulo: Jornal da Bahia – article by Jorge Amado
4.descricao: Political and civil proceeding No. H-5-4-6, opened by the Overseas Ministry, General Directorate of Political and Civil Administration, involving the Brazilian writer Jorge Amado and Professor Agostinho da Silva. It includes an open letter by Agostinho da Silva, published in the newspaper Voz de Portugal (Rio de Janeiro), and Jorge Amado’s reply, published in Jornal da Bahia. The articles discuss the direction of Brazilian and Angolan foreign policy in 1963.
4.area: Angola, Brazil, Anti-colonial struggles, Politics, History, Central Africa

5.titulo: Uses and Customs of Angola, by Oscar Ribas
5.descricao: Political and civil proceeding No. Z-1, opened by the Overseas Ministry, General Directorate of Political and Civil Administration, approving the publication and circulation of the book “Uso e Costumes de Angola” by Oscar Ribas, published by the University of Bahia in 1965.

6.titulo: Social and Cultural Crusade of Black Brazilians
6.descricao: Political and civil proceeding No. H-5-4-12, opened by the Overseas Ministry, General Directorate of Political and Civil Administration. It comprises three documents: a communication from the Portuguese Embassy in Kinshasa on discontent within the Congolese National Army; a telegram from the General Government of Angola on the visit of Dr. Silva Ribeiro and Mr. Serafim Araújo, Brazilian representatives of the company Braso/África; and correspondence between Dr. A. Agostinho Neto and José da Silva Oliveira, representative of the “Social and Cultural Crusade of Black Brazilians” (based in São Paulo), reporting the Crusade’s support against the unjust imprisonment of Rev. Father Pinto de Andrade in Angola.
6.area: Politics, Angola, Central Africa, Congolese National Army

7.descricao: Proceeding No. H-5-4-1, opened by the Overseas Ministry, Office of Political Affairs. It gathers several newspaper clippings on the organization of the Afro-Luso-Brazilian community, involving Angola, Mozambique and Portugal, focused on political events surrounding the 1964 military coup in Brazil.

8.titulo: Miscellaneous documents on the Center for Afro-Oriental Studies of the University of Bahia.
8.descricao: Set of official letters, regulations and newspaper clippings on the activities of the Center for Afro-Oriental Studies (CEAO), linked to the Federal University of Bahia, dated between 1961 and 1971: creation of the Brazilian Institute of Afro-Asian Studies within CEAO (mediated by Professors Agostinho da Silva and Waldir Freitas de Oliveira); Professor Waldir de Oliveira taking office as director of CEAO; African political refugee students on exchange; research by Prof. Vivaldo da Costa Lima on the Portuguese presence on the West African coast; courses and lectures with Asian and African professors; Prof. Waldir Oliveira’s participation in the 1st International Congress of Africanists (Ghana); the writer Oscar Ribas in Brazil and at CEAO-Bahia; articles by Professor Agostinho da Silva on CEAO and on customs in Macau; and the lecture “The situation of women in Angola”, given at CEAO by the political refugee Maria Archer.
8.area: Brazil, Central Africa, Afro-Luso-Brazilian Community, CEAO, Military Dictatorship, International Congress of Africanists, International Relations

9.titulo: West-Central Africa in the 19th century (c.1850-1890): exchange with the outside world – appropriation, exploration and documentation.
9.descricao: Publication by Beatrix Heintze, 2013, by Kilombelombe Publishers, Luanda/Angola. Includes the table of contents, preface and part four, chapter X – In the chameleon’s tracks: early ethnographic photography of Angola in context.

10.titulo: Ethnic distribution of the province of Angola
10.descricao: Ethnography by José Redinha, published by the Angola Information and Tourism Center. It records ethnic groups of Bantu-speaking peoples (Kikongo, Kimbundu, Lunda-Kioko, Umbundu, Ganguela, Nhaneka-Humbe, Ambó, Herero and Xindonga) and non-Bantu-speaking peoples (Khoikhoi-San and Vatua), with an ethnic map of the province of Angola.

11.titulo: Portuguese explorers and African kings: journeys to the heart of Africa in the 19th century.
11.descricao: Publication by ethnologist Frederico Delgado Rosa and anthropologist Filipe Verde, by A Esfera dos Livros, on the exploration of Africa through travelers’ accounts. Includes the index, prologue, part one – The explorers and their labyrinth: Portugal, Africa and the Europeans in the 19th century (chapters 1 to 4), iconography, epilogue, notes and bibliography.

12.titulo: We, the Cabindas: history, laws, uses and customs of the peoples of N’Goio.
12.descricao: Contains the text of the Treaty of Simulambuco, of February 1, 1885, concerning the Kingdom of Cabinda. Ethnography written by Prince D. Domingos José Franque – Boma Zanei-N’Vimba, published in 1940 by Editora Arco, Lisbon, on the history, laws, uses and customs of the peoples of N’Goio in the Kingdom of Cabinda.

13.titulo: The East and America: notes on the uses and customs of the peoples of Portuguese India compared with those of Brazil
13.descricao: Notes from the 1892 International Congress of Orientalists, held by the Lisbon Geographical Society. Record of a paper presented at the first session, organized by A. Lopes Mendes and published by the Imprensa Nacional de Lisboa, on marriages, funerals, the discovery of Brazil, and Luso-Brazilians and Spanish Americans.
13.area: Ethnography, Portuguese India, The East, America, Brazil

14.descricao: Work organized by Lisbon judge F.A. Pinto, 1888, published by Livraria Ferreira Editora. Includes the introduction, preface and index of the Third Lecture (“Ethnography”), with ethnographic descriptions of food, smoking, body ornaments, clothing, fine arts, property, religion, morals, death, social organization, war, inquimba fetish, industry and improvidence, as well as maps of Angola and Congo drawn in 1885.

15.titulo: Africans in Portugal: History and memory: 15th-21st centuries
15.descricao: Catalog of the exhibition “Africans in Portugal: History and Memory – 15th-21st Centuries”, held at the Belém Tower from May 4 to June 5, 2011, written by Isabel Castro Henriques and published by the Portuguese Committee of the UNESCO project “The Slave Route”. Texts in Portuguese and English; includes the index, introduction, chapters on continuities and changes (18th-19th centuries) and new African dynamics (after 1974), as well as references.

16.descricao: Work by David Birmingham, historian specializing in the modern history of Central Africa and Angola, professor emeritus of History at the University of Kent. Published by Editora Vega in 2003, translated and introduced by Arlindo Barbeitos. Highlights chapter 5 – Traditions, migrations and cannibalism, on the traditions of the Kingdom of Kongo in the 16th century. Also includes the table of contents, chapter 5 footnotes and the book’s flap.
16.area: History of Angola, Kingdom of Kongo, 16th Century, History of Africa

17.descricao: Work by James Duffy, American scholar who taught at Brandeis University, specialist in African studies, Portuguese colonial history and literature. Published in 1962 by Penguin Books, with a preface by Ronald Segal (activist and founder of the anti-apartheid magazine Africa South and of the Penguin African Library). It covers colonial history in Central Africa from the 16th to the 20th century (preface, introduction and part 1 – The Past: Portugal and Congo; and Angola). Published in English.
17.area: History of Africa, History of Angola, History of the Congo

18.descricao: Publication by André Gonçalves Pereira (Portuguese law professor and lawyer) in the Revista do Gabinete de Estudos Ultramarinos, Lisbon, 1956. It discusses the concept of nationalism in relation to philosophy, Christianity and international law; analyzes forms and causes of African nationalism (racial discrimination, egalitarian ideas, national consciousness, economic causes, anti-colonial propaganda); and addresses nationalist movements in northwest Africa, the Gold Coast, Togo and Kenya.
18.area: Nationalism, History of West Africa, History of East Africa, International Relations

19.titulo: Territory and Identity: the construction of colonial Angola (c.1872 – c.1926)
19.descricao: Work by Portuguese historian Isabel Castro Henriques on the construction of colonial identity in Angola between the late 19th century and the first decades of the 20th, published by the Center for History of the University of Lisbon in 2004. Highlights chapter 4 – Iconography, on the use of iconography of the land and of African territories and the fabrication of colonial territory (from cartography to the construction of new landscapes). Includes the references consulted and the full index.
19.area: History of Africa, History of Colonial Angola, 19th and 20th Centuries

20.titulo: Bulletin of the General Government of the Province of Angola. No. 93 of 19 Jun 1847.
20.descricao: Ordinance on the Provisional Regulations for the Luanda Prison – up to article 7, paragraph 24.

21.titulo: Bulletin of the General Government of the Province of Angola. No. 94 of 26 Jun 1847.
21.descricao: Ordinance on the Provisional Regulations for the Luanda Prison – covering articles 8 to 11.

22.titulo: Official Bulletin of the General Government of the Province of Angola. No. 96 of 10 Jul 1847.
22.descricao: Establishment of a commission to fill the interim post of Clerk of the Court in the District of Luanda. Civil section, prize court and maritime news.

23.titulo: Official Bulletin of the General Government of the Province of Angola. No. 100 of 07 Aug 1847.
23.descricao: Notices in the civil section on changes in the post of Court Clerk in the province of Luanda; on timber construction in the province of Barra do Bengo; auctions of enslaved Africans at the Luanda Customs House; notices on abandoned and deceased enslaved people in the province of Angola; auction of foodstuffs.

24.titulo: Official Bulletin of the General Government of the Province of Angola. No. 119 of 18 Dec 1847.
24.descricao: Appointment of Balthazar da Silva e Souza as public teacher of first letters – Primary Instruction Teacher in Máxima, including instructions for teaching classes. Notices on the Prize Court and seized brigs (vessels).
24.area: Education, Teaching and Slavery in Angola.

25.titulo: Official Bulletin of the Colony of Angola. Series I. Supplement to issue 29. 05 Aug 1937.
25.descricao: Ordinance No. 2,383 on legislation governing the exercise of press freedom in the colonies.

26.titulo: Official Bulletin of the Colony of Angola. Series I. Issue 31. 14 Aug 1937.
26.descricao: Decree No. 27,859 creating, within the Ministry of the Colonies, a film mission to the African Colonies of the Empire, intended to prepare and produce propaganda documentaries highlighting the civilizing effort of the Portuguese.

27.titulo: Official Bulletin of Angola. Series I. Issue 9. 27 Feb 1965.
27.descricao: Decree No. 45,498 enacting the Regulations of the Portuguese Honorific Orders.
27.area: International Relations, Culture, Science, Technology and Education.

28.titulo: Official Bulletin of Angola. Series I. Issue 31. 31 Jul 1965.
28.descricao: Ordinance No. 13,867 of the Luanda Institute of Scientific Research creating primary schools (school posts) in several districts, namely: Benguela, Bié, Cabinda, Cuando Cubango, Cuanza-Norte, Cuanza-Sul, Luanda, Lunda, Malange, Moçâmedes and Moxico.

29.titulo: Catalog of Documents on Military Expeditions to Angola and Mozambique in the First World War
29.descricao: Three hundred storage units were identified for the Military Expedition to Angola, with documents dated between 1914 and 1919, and one thousand and eighty units for Mozambique, with documents from 1914 to 1922, including the activity of the Mozambique Expeditionary Corps, held in Cape Verde between 1917 and 1918. Particularly significant are the records of the Health Services, the Transport Company, the Engineering Services and the Headquarters Intelligence Service.
29.area: First World War, Military Expeditions, Angola, Mozambique.

30.titulo: Inventory of Documents of the Banco Nacional Ultramarino
30.descricao: Inventory of administrative documents (correspondence, registration of securities/shares, consignments, among others), as well as accounting books (journal, ledger, cash book, balance sheets, among others).

31.titulo: General Inventory of the AHU’s Printed Cartography
31.descricao: Inventory of historical and geographical maps covering the Kingdom of Portugal, the Azores, Cape Verde, Guinea, São Tomé, Angola, Mozambique, India, Macau, Timor, Africa, Asia, America, Europe, Europe-British Isles, Australia, Seas and Oceans.
31.area: Cartography, Geography, History, Europe, Asia, Africa, America, Oceania.

32.titulo: Manuscript Cartography of Brazil at the AHU
32.descricao: Catalog of manuscript cartography of Brazil containing maps, geographic charts, plans and topographies.
32.area: Cartography of Brazil, Geography of Brazil, History of Brazil.

33.titulo: General Manuscript Cartography of the AHU
33.descricao: Catalog of cartography covering the Kingdom of Portugal, Madeira, the Azores, Cape Verde, Guinea, São João Batista de Ajudá, São Tomé and Príncipe, Angola, Mozambique, India, Macau, Timor, Sea Routes, Europe, Africa (North, West, Central, Southern, East), Asia, America, China.
33.area: Cartography, Geography, History, Europe, Asia, Africa, America, Oceania.

34.titulo: Catalog of Loose Manuscript Documents concerning Bahia-LF held at the AHU
34.descricao: Inventory of loose manuscript documents such as petitions, royal letters, receipts, certificates, contracts, charters and regulations, among other types. Miscellaneous Manuscripts – Shelfmark: AHU_CU_005-02, Cx., D.

35.titulo: Catalog of Loose Manuscript Documents concerning the Captaincy of Bahia held at the AHU
35.descricao: Inventory of loose manuscript documents such as petitions, royal letters, receipts, certificates, contracts, charters and regulations, among other types. Miscellaneous Manuscripts – Shelfmark: AHU_ACL_CU_005, Cx., D.

36.titulo: Catalog of Loose Manuscript Documents concerning Bahia-CA held at the AHU
36.descricao: Inventory of loose manuscript documents such as petitions, royal letters, receipts, certificates, contracts, charters and regulations, among other types. Miscellaneous Manuscripts – Shelfmark: AHU_CU_005-01, Cx., D.

37.titulo: Partial Catalog of Loose Manuscript Documents concerning Angola held at the AHU
37.descricao: Inventory of loose manuscript documents such as petitions, royal letters, receipts, certificates, contracts, charters and regulations, among other types. It is a series of loose documents on Angola from the Overseas Council archive, describing and organizing documents dated between the 17th and 19th centuries. Miscellaneous Manuscripts – Shelfmark: AHU_CU_001, Cx., D.

38.titulo: Inventory of Documents of the Overseas Ministry, Minister’s Office – Office of Political Affairs
38.descricao: About 175 m of records from the Political Affairs Department of the Office of Political Affairs of the Overseas Ministry were transferred in 1997 and 1999 from the Secretariat of State for Public Administration at the Palácio das Laranjeiras to the Overseas Historical Archive at the Palácio da Ega. They include documents such as reports, correspondence, registers, confidential/secret copies, telegrams, certificates and forms, among other types. Angola, Mozambique and Macau are the main countries/regions covered by these documents.

39.titulo: Catalog of Manuscript Iconography held at the AHU
39.descricao: Catalog of ethnographies, coats of arms, flags, fauna, flora and ships, covering the Kingdom of Portugal, Madeira, the Azores, Cape Verde, Guinea, São Tomé and Príncipe, Angola, Mozambique, India, Macau, Timor, Africa, Asia, China, Brazil.

40.titulo: Catalog of Printed Iconography held at the AHU
40.descricao: Iconographic catalog with 2,778 items (buildings, regions, ethnographies, ships, coats of arms, flags, machines, among others), covering Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania and America.
40.area: Iconography of Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania and America.

41.titulo: Cartography Commission 1883-1936: Partial Inventory of the AHU
41.descricao: The initial corpus consisted of 370 bundles, selected by the transfer note from the Overseas Registry of the Overseas Ministry to the Overseas Historical Archive (Note 37 of 1937) and identified as coming from the archive of the Cartography Commission. Of this set, 22 bundles, mostly concerning Mozambique, could not be located. The subjects vary over time according to the Commission’s responsibilities: cartography and geographical studies of colonial territories; geographical and scientific missions; astronomy, geodesy, hydrography and meteorology; border demarcation; navigation and merchant navy; relations with the Colonial Geological Museum; colonial naval services; diplomatic and consular affairs.

42.titulo: The civilizing mission of the State in Angola. Part III. Published by the Centro Tipográfico Colonial in Lisbon.
42.descricao: Ethnography by José de Oliveira Ferreira Diniz (Provincial Secretary of Angola) discussing the civilizing process in Angola through education, immigration and the organization of “native” affairs. Divided into three parts; only the introduction and part III, on the instruments indispensable to the State’s civilizing mission, were collected. Bibliographic reference: pages 93-119.

43.titulo: Bantu Africa. Races and tribes of Angola. Printed by Oficinas Fernandes, Lisbon.
43.descricao: Study by Luiz Figueira in 1938 on the races and tribes inhabiting the colony of Angola, their uses, customs, ways of life, dialects, medicinal plants and poisons. It covers aspects of the arts, religion and animism, with monographs on Angola, Congo, Luanda and Lunda. Bibliographic reference: pages 5-36 and 266-327.

44.descricao: Publication by Anselmo Ferraz de Carvalho, Coimbra Editora, 1943, addressing aspects of the geology and geography of Angola from a perspective comparative with Brazil. Bibliographic reference: pages 5-12.

45.titulo: Angola: notes on the occupation and early settlement of the Portuguese in Congo, Angola and Benguela.
45.descricao: Printed source drawn from historical documents on Portuguese colonial history, published by the Coimbra University Press in 1933 and organized by Alfredo de Albuquerque Felner. Includes the index and appendix 46 – Account of the uses and customs of the people of Congo by the Bishop of Angola.

46.descricao: Studies by Manoel Alfredo de Morais Maris, of the Higher Institute of Overseas Studies, in 1958, published by the Overseas Ministry. Includes the preface, introduction, chapters 1 and 2 (Religious institutions), final remarks and bibliography, analyzing economic, social and religious aspects before and after contact with the Portuguese colonizer.

47.titulo: On the importance of Bantu studies for understanding Brazilian socio-cultural issues.
47.descricao: Text by Augusto Guilherme Mesquitela Lima, part of the Proceedings of the 5th International Colloquium of Luso-Brazilian Studies (Coimbra), on the importance of Bantu studies for understanding Brazilian socio-cultural issues.

48.titulo: Ethnography of Angola (Southwest and Center). Collection of scattered articles. Volume 1.
48.descricao: Ethnography organized by Carlos Estermann, Lutheran missionary in Angola, published by the Tropical Scientific Research Institute. Includes the index, a biographical summary of Carlos Estermann, prologue, presentation and chapters I, II, XXI and XXIII, on ethnic differentiation in Southwest and Central Angola.

49.titulo: Ethnography of Angola (Southwest and Center). Collection of scattered articles. Volume 2.
49.descricao: Ethnography organized by Carlos Estermann, Lutheran missionary in Angola, published by the Tropical Scientific Research Institute. Includes the index and chapter I – The Angola Mission and Bantu worship, spirit worship and magic.

50.titulo: Ethnography of the peoples of Angola. Tome I
50.descricao: Ethnography organized by the Portuguese Republic, General Government of Angola/Secretariat of Native Affairs, published by the Imprensa Nacional de Luanda. It addresses the uses and customs of the Black/Bantu native population, covering chapters 1 Ngolas, 2 Dembos and 3 Muchicongos, with general ethnographic characteristics, material and intellectual life, and family and social organization.

51.titulo: Umbundu Grammar: the language of central Angola
51.descricao: Ethnography by Fr. José Francisco Valente, contributor to the Bantu languages section of the Ethnology and Ethnography Division of the Angola Institute of Scientific Research. Includes the presentation, prologue and section three (Syntax), covering principles and methods of the language, proverbs, and an analysis of area and dialects.

52.descricao: Ethnography organized by Oscar Ribas and published by the Museum of Angola, devoted to studies of Black religion and religiosity in Angola. Includes preliminaries and chapters on deities, ministers of worship, divination and a section with engravings.

53.descricao: Ethnography organized by Mario Milheiros and published by the Angola Institute of Scientific Research. It addresses ethnolinguistic typologies (groups and subgroups) and, in chapter II, the study of Religion: superstitions, spells, ceremonies, sorcerers, funeral ceremonies, graves and mourning.
53.area: Ethnography, Ethnology, Ethnolinguistics, Religion, Witchcraft, Funeral rites.

54.titulo: The Africans: an introduction to their cultural history
54.descricao: Ethnography by Basil Davidson, published by the African Studies Library, Edições 70, Lisbon, covering religious structures in Angola (part III of the source): science as social control, witches, sorcerers and magic, in sections X to XVIII.
54.area: Ethnography, Ethnology, Religion, Witchcraft, Magic, Sorcery.

55.descricao: Ethnography by Eduardo dos Santos, published as an offprint of Revista Ultramar, in five parts: the Bantu, their names and migrations; religion as a concept; against factions of religion; monotheism; messianic political movements; and a brief conclusion.
55.area: Ethnography, Ethnology, Religion, Bantu Peoples, Angola.

56.titulo: Ethnographic contributions to the history of the peoples of Angola
56.descricao: Ethnography by João Vicente Martins, Portuguese Republic, Overseas Ministry, published by the Publications and Library Division of the General Overseas Agency. It covers phonetics, spelling, syllables, phonetic tables and proverbs.

57.titulo: Dancing to the sound of the batuque in Mozambique
57.descricao: Record of a community dancing to the sound of the batuque in Mozambique in 1935.

58.descricao: Record of a community dancing to the sound of the batuque in Mozambique in 1935.
58.area: Customs, Witchcraft, Religiosity, East Africa, Mozambique

59.descricao: Record of a community dancing to the sound of the batuque in Mozambique in 1935.

60.descricao: Newspaper A Época, 26.08.1921. Addressed to the “liberals” of the “Union”. Reactionary Brazil! Catholic statements by Mr. Arthur Bernardes, president of the State of Minas Gerais and candidate for the presidency of the Republic.
60.area: Religion, Catholic religious ideology in Brazil, Religious freedom, Brazilian Republic

61.titulo: Discussions on religion in Brazil from clippings of the newspaper A Época – Lisbon
61.descricao: Newspaper A Época, 17.11.1922, report on Arthur Bernardes after his election as president of Brazil and his Catholic religious ideology.
61.area: Religion, Catholic religious ideology in Brazil, Religious freedom, Brazilian Republic

62.titulo: The separation of Church and State in Brazil (from Ruy Barbosa’s historical eulogy)
62.descricao: Newspaper A Época, 6.04.1923. Discussions on religion in Brazil from newspaper clippings. Partial text of Decree No. 119 A of January 7, 1890.
62.area: Religion, Catholic religious ideology in Brazil, Religious freedom, Brazilian Republic

63.titulo: The Church and the Brazilian republic
63.descricao: Newspaper A Época, 29.07.1924. Discussions on religion in Brazil from newspaper clippings.
63.area: Religion, Catholic religious ideology in Brazil, Religious freedom, Brazilian Republic

64.titulo: Religious freedom in Brazil, according to Dr. Bettencourt Rodrigues. Newspaper A Época – Lisbon
64.descricao: Newspaper A Época, 6.04.1926. Discussions on religion in Brazil from newspaper clippings.
64.area: Religion, Catholic religious ideology in Brazil, Religious freedom, Brazilian Republic

65.titulo: Missions of Angola and Congo. Newspaper A Época, Lisbon
65.descricao: Newspaper Época, 31.01.1925: The collapse of the religious missions in Angola was a disastrous mistake (includes a photo of a civilized Christian couple and a map of the Protestant missions in Angola in 1912).

66.titulo: Elements on the Jinga ethnic group
66.descricao: Special Intelligence Report No. 19, book 190, organized by the Angola Intelligence Centralization and Coordination Service (SCCIA). It analyzes historical aspects, territory, social and political organization, customary law, religion and beliefs of the Jinga, as well as political aspects labeled “subversive”. Report written by Renato Prerestelo Vieira, head of an SCCIA district delegation.
66.area: Ethnography, Angola, Jinga, History of Africa, 20th c.

67.titulo: Elements on the Ovimbundu ethnic group
67.descricao: Special Intelligence Report No. 23, book 193, organized by the Angola Intelligence Centralization and Coordination Service (SCCIA). It analyzes history, trade, language, customs, territory, social and political organization, religion and magic.
67.area: Ethnography, Angola, Ovimbundu, History of Africa, 20th c.

68.titulo: Elements on the Kikongo ethnic group
68.descricao: Special Intelligence Report No. 22, book 192, organized by the Angola Intelligence Centralization and Coordination Service (SCCIA). It analyzes history, territory, economy, social aspects, traditional institutions, myths, sects, prophetic-messianic associations and the personality of the Congolese peoples. Study by ethnographer José Redinha.
68.area: Ethnography, Angola, Kikongo, History of Africa, 20th c.

69.titulo: Censorship record of the film “Sortilégio Africano”
69.descricao: Proceeding on the censorship of the film “Chikwembo – Sortilégio Africano” (African Spell), a drama by Portuguese producer Felipe Selms. It was authorized with cuts so that it would be shown to adults only. The initial rating would have allowed viewers aged 12 and over. After cuts to lines with expressions such as kill, spell, murderer, crime, relentless poison, coward and a woman’s honesty, the film was released for viewers over 13.

70.titulo: Books authorized in Lisbon addressing African topics
70.descricao: Mandinka Customs; Life, religion and death of the Mandinka, both by António Carreira, 1942. Ethnologist, writer and colonial administrator. His analyses cover the customs and traditions of peoples in the region of Guinea and Cape Verde.
70.area: African Literature, Mandinka, African colonization, Brazilian Literature

71.titulo: Book authorized in Lisbon addressing African topics
71.descricao: Black Kings, by Julião Quintinha, 1942, Portuguese journalist, writer and republican activist. He discussed colonial and African realities.
71.area: African Literature, Mandinka, African colonization, Brazilian Literature

72.titulo: Book censored in Lisbon addressing African topics
72.descricao: Bahia de Tous les Saints, by Jorge Amado, 1939. A writer from Bahia who sought to draw a kind of affective and ethnographic map of the city of Salvador. Portuguese censors disliked the way the Brazilian author described the Portuguese colonial profile.
72.area: African Literature, Mandinka, African colonization, Brazilian Literature

73.titulo: The history of Kongo and Angola revisited.
73.descricao: Work published by António Custódio Gonçalves, Portuguese sociologist and researcher in African studies in Portugal. Published by Estampa in 2005, it is composed of three parts: the first is entitled “At the origins of the encounter of peoples and cultures”, the second “Lineage dynamics of traditional power” and the third “Political change and social innovation”. From the first part we highlight section 1, “Crossroads of migrations” (pp. 33-53), as well as the general bibliography and appendices. Section 1 of the first part analyzes the origins and formation of the Mbanza Congo chieftaincy based on 16th- and 17th-century documents.
73.area: History of Central Africa, Congo, Angola, Mbanza Congo, Chiefs

74.titulo: Afro-Brazilian culture and politics: Bahia, 1790s to 1990s.
74.descricao: Work edited by Brazilianist historian Hendrik Kraay, published by M. E. Sharpe Inc. in 1998, discussing aspects of Afro-Brazilian culture and politics in Bahia from the 18th to the 20th century. Included here are Kraay’s introduction, chapter 7 “Between affliction and politics: a case study of Bahian candomblé” by French anthropologist Michel Agier, and the bibliography.
74.area: History of Brazil, Religion, Candomblé, Inter-ethnic relations, Race relations, 18th, 19th and 20th Centuries.

75.descricao: Ethnographic catalog published by the Institute of Anthropology of the University of Coimbra, Portugal, organized by researchers Maria Isilda Filgueiras and Marie-Luise Bastin, together with Miguel Ramos and Rui de Sousa Martins. It addresses material aspects of traditional Angolan cultures, especially the Tchokwe people. The chapters selected are on society and political power, musical arts, and man and the supernatural – an approach to divination, sculpture and African masks.

76.titulo: Angola: symbols of power in traditional society
76.descricao: Publication No. 1 (1983) of the Center for African Studies, part of the Institute of Anthropology of the University of Coimbra, organized by researchers Manuel Laranjeiras Rodrigues de Areia, Maria do Rosário Antunes Rodrigues Martins and Jacques Houart. It contains two specific articles: one by Mario Antonio Fernandes de Oliveira on insignia of power among the Cabindas from a historical-cultural perspective; and one by Carlos Moreira Henrique Serrano discussing power, symbols and the social imaginary in Bawoyo and Mangoyo societies.

77.titulo: The frontiers of spirits in Central Africa
77.descricao: Chapter by University of Lisbon historian Isabel Castro Henriques, part of the book “Uma vida em história: estudos em homenagem a António Borges Coelho”, published in 2001 by Caminho, Portugal. It discusses forms of ancestral religiosity in Central African territories along two themes: nature, spirit and human settlement; and the power of spirits in demarcating territories.
77.area: History of Africa, Central Africa, Ancestral religiosity.

78.titulo: Treasures hidden in a short article: “Famine and disease in the history of Angola (c.1830-1930)”, by Jill R. Dias
78.descricao: Chapter by Cristiana Bastos, researcher at the Institute of Social Sciences of the University of Lisbon, part of the book “As lições de Jill Dias: antropologia, história, África, academia”, published in 2013 by CRIA – Network Center for Research in Anthropology of the FCSH, Universidade Nova de Lisboa. The chapter highlights Jill Dias’s 1981 article in the Journal of African History on the intertwined history of Angolans and Portuguese regarding health, food and ecological constraints.

79.titulo: Bibliography of recent publications on Portuguese-speaking Africa.
79.descricao: Catalog of sources compiled in 1987 by the Revista Internacional de Estudos Africanos, Lisbon, containing general works on the history of colonial Portuguese Africa, literature, cooperation and development. It includes bibliographies on history, anthropology, sociology, literature, international development relations and economics for the following African countries: Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde, Angola, São Tomé and Príncipe and Mozambique. Also included are bibliographies from the Revista Internacional de Estudos Africanos, tables of contents of issues 1 to 7 (1984 to 1987).
79.area: Lusophone Africa, Anthropology, Sociology, History, International Relations, Economics.

80.descricao: Contains the table of contents, introduction and annotated bibliography of the book by anthropologist and professor of Brazilian culture Raul Lody, published in 1987 by Ática. It addresses the transculturation of the Ketu (Nagô), Jeje and Angola-Congo candomblé models to Brazil. It discusses candomblé as an emerging phenomenon and a space of African memory, and the presence of caboclo worship in terreiros. It also addresses the historical and anthropological neglect of candomblé originating among Bantu-speaking peoples, as well as the relations between religion, space and society.
80.area: Candomblé, Anthropology of Religion, African Heritage, Afro-Brazilian Religions.

81.titulo: Historical description of the three kingdoms of Congo, Matamba and Angola. Volume 1.
81.descricao: Printed bibliographic source published by the Overseas Research Board, Lisbon, in 1965. Organized by Fr. João António Cavazzi de Montecúccolo, volume 1. Book one contains the historical description of the kingdoms of Congo, Matamba and Angola, from the introduction of the work. There are also chapters on idolatry, sorcerers, oaths and other superstitions. We have also added chapters on dwellings, marriages, food, utensils, treatment of illnesses, means of communication, music and dance. Finally, a chapter on inheritance and slavery. The table of contents covers books 1 to 4.
81.area: History of Central Africa, Angola, Congo, Matamba, Ethnography.

82.titulo: Historical description of the three kingdoms of Congo, Matamba and Angola. Volume 2.
82.descricao: Printed bibliographic source published by the Overseas Research Board, Lisbon, in 1965. Organized by Fr. João António Cavazzi de Montecúccolo, volume 2. Only the table of contents of this volume, covering books 5, 6 and 7.
82.area: History of Central Africa, Angola, Congo, Matamba, Ethnography.

83.descricao: Printed sources organized by Mário António Fernandes de Oliveira and Carlos Alberto Mendes de Couto, members of the Angola Institute of Scientific Research, Luanda, and the Center for Overseas Historical Studies, Lisbon, published in 1971. The sources address relations with the Khoikhoi in the 19th century in southeastern Angola, according to letter No. 455/1884 from the Governor-General of Angola, Francisco Joaquim Ferreira do Amaral. It also includes document No. 01/1886, an annex to Letter No. 501/1886 issued by the governor of Moçâmedes, Álvaro da Costa Ferreira, on the Khoikhoi incursion into the port city of Moçâmedes, now Namibe.
83.area: Angola, Khoikhoi, History of Africa, 19th Century.

84.descricao: Printed source organized by Eduardo dos Santos, Portuguese researcher and missionary, in 1969, and published by the Overseas Research Board, Lisbon. Only the executive summary is included here. These are historical and anthropological studies on missionaries in Angola from the 16th to the 20th century. The records cover Catholicism, Protestantism, Adventists, archaic religions, syncretic movements and the Bahá’í Faith.
84.area: History of Religions, Angola, Christianity, African religions, Anthropology of Religion.

85.titulo: Images of the Sacred: between Paris Match and O Cruzeiro.
85.descricao: Work by Fernando Cury de Tacca, professor at the Arts Institute of Unicamp/SP. A contribution on the photographic coverage of Candomblé initiation rites in Salvador, Bahia, in 1951, when photos of the ritual processes were published in the magazines O Cruzeiro and Paris Match. Includes the table of contents, preface and introduction.

86.titulo: Black kings in slaveholding Brazil: history of the King of Congo coronation festival.
86.descricao: Work by Brazilian historian Marina de Mello e Souza, professor in the History Department of the University of São Paulo (USP). The author discusses the meanings of the coronation festivals and their connection with Central Africa, especially among the peoples of Congo and Angola. Her analysis considers Africans’ capacity to rebuild their identities even under slavery. Includes the table of contents, introduction and chapter III, “Peoples in contact: trade, power and identity”.
86.area: Cultural history, Popular festivals, King of Congo, African diaspora, Central Africa, Congo, Angola.

87.titulo: On the eve of the modern world: Africa. Vol. 1
87.descricao: Catalog published for the exhibition “On the Eve of the New World: Africa and Brazil”, held at the National Museum of Ethnology, Lisbon, during the first half of 1992. It was organized by the National Commission for the Commemoration of the Portuguese Discoveries, with text by anthropologist Jill R. Dias and translation by José Luís Luna. Volume 1, entitled Africa, covers Africa and Africans in the European imagination; early African objects in Europe; savanna and forest societies before the arrival of Europeans; Africa and the opening of the Atlantic; Benin, Congo and the Europeans. Besides the introduction, we highlight section III, Materials, cosmology and power, especially the discussion of the living and the dead.
87.area: Social and Cultural Anthropology, West-Central Africa, History of Africa.

88.titulo: New African identities in Angola in the context of Atlantic trade
88.descricao: Chapter XII of the book “Trânsitos coloniais: diálogos críticos luso-brasileiros” (eds. Cristiana Bastos, Miguel Vale de Almeida and Bela Feldman-Bianco), published in 2002 by the Institute of Social Sciences (ICS), Lisbon. In this text, British anthropologist based in Portugal Jill R. Dias analyzes how Africans and people of mixed descent in Angola (known as Ambaquistas) who had Western ways of life managed to emerge as colonial intermediaries in language, economy and culture, in relation both to Europeans and to society in the interior of Angola.

89.titulo: The Black Brazilian: religious ethnography and psychoanalysis
89.descricao: The work of Brazilian anthropologist Arthur Ramos is a landmark in studies of Afro-Brazilian culture, mapping rituals in candomblé terreiros of the Jeje-Nagô and Bantu groups. It uses psychoanalysis to understand behaviors, dreams and trance rites in terreiros in Bahia, Rio de Janeiro and Alagoas. The studies are presented here in two parts: first, the preface written in 1988 by anthropologist René Ribeiro for an edition published by Massangana in Recife; second, the first edition of the work, published by Civilização Brasileira in 1934 in Rio de Janeiro. The author presents his analysis in two parts, the first devoted to the study of Black “fetishist” religions and cults in Brazil and the second to psychoanalytic exegesis. Included here are the introduction and chapter IV, on cults of Bantu origin, along with the table of contents.

90.titulo: Black people in Portugal. 16th to 19th centuries
90.descricao: Catalog organized by the National Commission for the Commemoration of the Portuguese Discoveries in 1999, published by Textype Artes Gráficas. The catalog accompanies the exhibition held at the Jerónimos Monastery, Lisbon, in 1999-2000. It addresses Portugal before maritime and commercial expansion; faith and trade; expansion and trafficking; from slavery to freedom; and economic, social, religious and recreational life. It also addresses how white people viewed Black people, exchanges and influences, and highlights important figures. Only the chapter on religious life is included here.

91.titulo: Representations of Africa and Africans in history and culture, 15th to 21st centuries
91.descricao: Work organized by historians José Damião Rodrigues and Casimiro Rodrigues, published by CHAM – Center for Overseas History, School of Social Sciences and Humanities, Universidade Nova de Lisboa, 2011. It gathers texts from the Colloquium Representations of Africa and Africans in History and Culture, 15th to 21st Centuries, held in Ponta Delgada in 2009. The colloquium’s themes include African literature and culture, history of Africa, cultural representations and missionary work.
91.area: African Literature, African Culture, Cultural Representations, Missionary work, History of Africa.

92.titulo: The mystery of the orixás and the dolls: race and gender in Brazilian anthropology
92.descricao: Article by Brazilian anthropologist Mariza Corrêa, published in Etnográfica – Journal of the Network Center for Research in Anthropology, vol. 4(2), Lisbon, 2000. The author discusses how relations between race and gender took on new contours in Brazilian anthropology, including debates on miscegenation and the whitening theory.
92.area: Social Anthropology, Miscegenation, Race, Gender, Whitening, Candomblés.

93.titulo: Afro-Brazilian religions in Portugal: bruxos, priests and pais de santo
93.descricao: Article by Portuguese anthropologist Clara Saraiva, of Universidade Nova de Lisboa, published in Etnográfica – Journal of the Network Center for Research in Anthropology, vol. 14(2), pp. 265-288, 2010. The author discusses the immigration of Afro-Brazilian religions (candomblé, umbanda) to Portugal over the last twenty years. She examines how these religions attract Portuguese followers and the hermeneutic processes of influence circulating in the Africa-Brazil-Portugal triangle.
93.area: Candomblé, Umbanda, Syncretism, Transnational Religions, Immigration, Portugal.

94.titulo: Much ado about nothing, or the “xangô rezado baixo”: an ethnography of the “Quebra de 1912” in Alagoas, Brazil
94.descricao: Article by Ulisses Neves Rafael, Brazilian anthropologist at the Federal University of Sergipe, published in Etnográfica – Journal of the Network Center for Research in Anthropology, vol. 14(2), pp. 289-310, 2010. The author seeks to understand the fateful episode known in Alagoas as the “Quebra de 1912”, which resulted in the almost total destruction of Afro-religious houses of worship in the state capital and neighboring municipalities.
94.area: Ethnography, Religious persecution, Quebra de 1912, Xangô rezado baixo, Maceió-AL.

95.titulo: Clara Sarmento, Portuguese popular culture: practices, discourses and representations
95.descricao: An in-depth critical review by Portuguese anthropologist Ricardo Campos, professor at CEMRI – Universidade Aberta, published in Etnográfica – Journal of the Network Center for Research in Anthropology, vol. 14(1), pp. 206-208, 2010. The author analyzes Clara Sarmento’s book Cultura Popular Portuguesa: Práticas, Discursos e Representações, which won the 2007 CES Prize for Young Social Scientists of Portuguese-Speaking Countries.
95.area: Popular culture, Practices, Representations, Discourse, Review.

96.titulo: A question of identity: intellectual responses to economic change within the Creole elite of Portuguese Angola between 1870 and 1930
96.descricao: Article by anthropologist Jill R. Dias, published in the Revista Internacional de Estudos Africanos – I, 1984, organized by the Institute of African Studies and the Department of Anthropology of Universidade Nova de Lisboa. The author analyzes how Luanda’s Creole intellectual elite responded to the loss of economic power between 1870 and 1930.
96.area: Creole elite, Angola, Ethnography, History of Central Africa, Identities, Intellectuals.

97.titulo: Portuguese archives and the history of Africa
97.descricao: Article by anthropologist Jill R. Dias, published in the Revista Internacional de Estudos Africanos Nos. 18 and 22, 1995-1999, by the Center for African and Asian Studies of the Tropical Scientific Research Institute, Universidade Nova de Lisboa. The author analyzes the possibilities and limitations of colonial collections of historical sources, highlighting African agency. She cross-references colonial records with anthropological and material sources that help reconstruct Creole identities and pre-colonial structures.
97.area: Historical Archive, Colonial Collection, Documentation, History of Africa, Ethnography.

98.titulo: A happy misfortune [electronic document]: the image of Africa and Africans in missionary literature on Kongo and the Mbundu region (mid-16th c. – first quarter of the 18th c.)
98.descricao: PhD thesis in Anthropology by Carlos José Duarte Almeida, defended in 2009 at the School of Social Sciences and Humanities of Universidade Nova de Lisboa, supervised by Professors Jill R. Dias and Maria Cardeira da Silva. The study focuses on the image of Africa and Africans reflected in missionary literature on Kongo and the Mbundu region between the mid-16th and mid-18th centuries. It analyzes representations of the natural world and their connection with anthropological discourse.
98.area: Angola, Missionaries, Jesuits, Capuchins, Representation of Africans, Difference and Otherness.

99.titulo: Black and white [mimeographed text]: how the Portuguese expressed the structure of their culture in the ways they related to Africans
99.descricao: The 1999 dissertation “Preto e branco: de como os portugueses expressaram a estrutura da sua cultura nas modalidades do seu relacionamento com os africanos” by Maria Belo was defended at the Department of Portuguese Studies of the School of Social Sciences and Humanities, Universidade Nova de Lisboa. The author analyzes Portuguese identity and the construction of the colonial imaginary, showing how Portugal projected its worldview, values and social, political and religious structures in its relations with African peoples. It is a psychoanalytic study of Portuguese cultural specificity, including an interpretation of the “mirror stage” as a civilizational structure rooted in the formation of personality through the gaze of the Other.
99.area: Portuguese culture, African culture, Africa, Comparative psychology, Psychoanalysis, Race, Sexuality, Fetishism, Miscegenation

100.titulo: The construction of the world: religion, representations, ideology
100.descricao: Work organized by French ethnologist and anthropologist Marc Augé with other authors. The book examines African cosmologies and beliefs to unravel the complex relationship between the individual, social coercion, ideology and violence, focusing on practices and institutions, theories and representations. Selected here are the introduction, chapter II – “The notion of the person” by Françoise Michel-Jones, and chapter III – “Beliefs in witchcraft” by Marc Augé.
100.area: Social and cultural anthropology, Magic, Politics, Religion, Cosmology, Primitive societies

101.descricao: A list of anthropological sources organized by the Center for African Studies of the Institute of Anthropology of the University of Coimbra. The sources were compiled by Portuguese researchers M. L. Rodrigues de Areia and Isilda Figueiras in 1984. Only 4 pages out of 165 were selected.

102.titulo: Cultures of the lusophone Black Atlantic
102.descricao: “Cultures of the lusophone Black Atlantic” was edited by Nancy Priscilla Naro, Roger Sansi-Roca and David H. Treece and published by Palgrave Macmillan, New York, in 2007. The topics are distributed in three parts: the first on colonial formations; the second on migrations and colonial cultures; and the third on hybridity, multiculturalism and racial politics. Includes the table of contents and the introduction.
102.area: Latin America, Portuguese colonialism, Migrations, Brazil, Portuguese-speaking African countries (PALOP), Portugal, Identity, Religion, Syncretism, Hybridity, Multiculturalism.

103.descricao: Publication organized by Portuguese historian Valentim Alexandre, published in 2000 by Edições Colibri, Institute of Contemporary History of Universidade Nova de Lisboa. It discusses the colonial question as a central theme of contemporary Portuguese history. Besides the preface, it includes the chapters “The African empire (19th and 20th centuries) – an overview” by Valentim Alexandre; “Portuguese relations with African societies in Angola in the 19th century” by Jill R. Dias; and “Angola in the 20th century until 1974” by Maria da Conceição Neto.
103.area: African empire, 19th Century, 20th Century, History of Africa, Portuguese colonization, Angola, São Tomé and Príncipe, Mozambique.

104.titulo: European views of Angola: occupation of the territory, military operations, knowledge of the peoples, modernization projects (1883-1918). Anthology of period texts.
104.descricao: An anthology of period texts organized by João Freire, Portuguese sociologist, writer and professor at ISCTE, Lisbon. The collection was published in 2011 by the Navy Cultural Commission, Edições Culturais da Marinha. Besides the index and general presentation, it includes section A of chapter 1, part 6 – COUTINHO, Carlos Viegas Gago. Impressions of two journeys across Africa between Angola and Mozambique, 1915.
104.area: Colonial administration, Colonial policy, Portuguese colonies, Angola, 19th and 20th Centuries, Anthologies.

105.descricao: Sketch map of Angola, Luanda and Congo, No. 9 (sketch). Cartographic material. Cartography Commission. 1917 edition. Scale 1:2,000,000. [Lisbon: Ministry of the Colonies], 1917. 1 map: color; 43.20x37.50 cm, on a 55.00x45.00 cm sheet. Lower margin note: “N.B. The Malange railway from Xissa to Tabango, near the border on the Kasai, is planned to pass through Quinzunzo and near Capenda Camalemba.” Author and data attributed according to “Atlas colonial português, no. 9”. Includes a 100 km scale bar.

106.titulo: Whites and Blacks in Bahia: a study of racial contact / Donald Pierson. 2nd ed. – São Paulo: Comp. Editora Nacional, 1971.
106.descricao: Only the references to Bahian newspapers consulted by Donald Pierson, found on page 341 of the work.

122.descricao: Religious Missions in the life of the colony.
122.area: Discourses on Customs in Central Africa

123.titulo: Description of the Dress of the Blacks of the coast of Angola / [Louis Ohier de Grandpré]
123.descricao: Manuscript describing the dress, customs and dwellings of the Black people of the coast of Angola. Text written by the Count of Grandpré in the 18th century. The document is written in French and has not been translated.
123.area: Document on Customs in the Congo, Central Africa

124.titulo: The Savage and the Exotic: a contribution to a critical reorganization of the historical reading of the populations of Southwest Angola (19th-20th centuries).
124.descricao: Master’s dissertation (table of contents and introduction only) by Eunice Maria Rodrigues Costa Marques Luís, University of Lisbon. A critique of the historical reading of the populations of Southwest Angola between the late 19th century and the first half of the 20th century.
124.area: History of Africa, Southwest Angola, 19th c., 20th c.

125.titulo: Nation-building in Africa. The examples of Angola, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique and São Tomé and Príncipe
125.descricao: Several papers presented at the INEP/CODESRIA/UNITAR Colloquium, published in 1989. Two articles were selected: “Nation formation and ethno-cultural identities” by Eduardo J. Barros (pp. 77-94); and “Notes on the national question in Angola” by Henrique Abranches (pp. 129-169). Published by the National Institute for Studies and Research of Guinea-Bissau. The file also contains the publication’s table of contents.
125.area: Nation, Nationalism, Lusophony, Angola, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, São Tomé and Príncipe

126.descricao: Essay by A. Borges de Melo, 1992, published by Mundinter Editora. Excerpts selected to contextualize Brazil’s influence on the history and development of the press in Angola, especially throughout the 20th century.

127.titulo: Brief notes on cultural integration in Angola.
127.descricao: Essay resulting from a dialogue between Domingos Van-Dúnem and Ruy Burity da Silva, organized for the 6th Conference of Afro-Asian Writers (1979) in agreement with the Union of Angolan Writers. It seeks to reinterpret the historical relations between the country’s different peoples and cultures, based on guidelines of the MPLA-Labour Party and the People’s Republic of Angola.
127.area: Angola, Culture, Anti-colonial literature, History of Africa

128.titulo: Candomblé in Portuguese: history, organization, theology.
128.descricao: Work by Portuguese anthropologist of religion and writer João Ferreira Dias, addressing the history, theology and organization of candomblé, especially the Ketu tradition. It discusses the dynamics of the diaspora and the adaptation of candomblé and other religions of African origin, such as umbanda, to the sociocultural context of Portugal. The preface and chapter 1, “Origins”, were selected.

129.descricao: Publication by Leonel Cosme, Portuguese poet, fiction writer, essayist and publisher, with reflections on cultural and intellectual life in Angola during the colonial and post-independence periods. The introduction and the chapter “Racial motivations in Angola” were selected.
